questions.question: What is the aim of fundamental rights mentioned in the Indian Constitution?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**To establish political democracy.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The aim of **fundamental rights** mentioned in the Indian Constitution is to establish **political democracy. **
 
• Fundamental rights are the** basic rights **that every citizen of India is entitled to.
 
• These rights are essential for the development of a **democratic society.**
 
• The fundamental rights are enshrined in the Constitution to ensure that the citizens have the freedom to** express their views, form associations, and participate in the governance** of the country.
 
• The aim of fundamental rights is to establish political democracy by ensuring that every citizen has the** right to vote,** and the right to participate in the** decision-making process** of the government.
 
• The fundamental rights also ensure that the citizens have the **right to life, liberty, and equality before the law**, which are essential for the functioning of a democratic society.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **To establish a welfare state:**

 
 
• While the aim of fundamental rights is to establish a welfare state, it is** not **the primary aim.
 
• The primary aim is to establish **political democracy.**
 
 
 
• **To have absolute independence:**
 
 
• This option is not correct as the aim of fundamental rights is** not **to promote absolute independence but to ensure that citizens have the freedom to express their **views and participate** in the governance of the country.
 
 
 
• **To promote economic justice:**
 
 
• While economic justice is an important aspect of fundamental rights, it is **not** the primary aim.
 
• The primary aim is to establish **political democracy.**

questions.question: Which of the following Articles of the Indian Constitution mentions the right to form co-operative societies?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**19 (1) (c).**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The 97th Constitutional Amendment Act of 2011 gave constitutional status and protection to cooperative societies.
 
• In this context, it made the following three changes in the Constitution:
 
 
• It made the right to form cooperative societies a fundamental right (Article 19).
 
• It included a new Directive Principle of State Policy on the promotion of cooperative societies (Article 43-B).
 
• It added a new Part IX-B in the Constitution which is entitled “The Cooperative Societies” (Articles 243-ZH to 243-ZT).
 
 
 
• The new Part IX-B contains various provisions to ensure that the cooperative societies in the country function in a democratic, professional, autonomous, and economically sound manner.
 
• It empowers the Parliament in respect of multi-state cooperative societies and the state legislatures in respect of other cooperative societies to make the appropriate law.
 
• Article 43B deals with the promotion of cooperative societies. The State shall endeavor to promote voluntary formation, autonomous functioning, democratic control, and professional management of co-operative societies. [Article 43B Inserted by the 97th Constitution Amendment Act, 2011].

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• 97th Amendment Act, 2011

 
 
• The right to form cooperative societies is a fundamental right that has been provided in the Indian Constitution.
 
• It is enshrined in Article 19(c) of the Constitution, which guarantees the freedom to form associations or unions.
 
• This right was added to the Constitution by the 97th Amendment Act of 2011.
 
• Article 19(1)(c) guarantees all citizens the right "to form associations or unions or co-operative societies".
 
• However, this right, like other rights under Article 19, is not absolute and is subject to reasonable restrictions under clause (4) of the same article, namely "in the interests of the sovereignty and integrity of India, the security of the State, friendly relations with foreign States, public order or morality or in relation to contempt of court, defamation or incitement to an offence".

questions.question: The Fundamental Rights have been guaranteed to protect the public from repressive state actions; judicial decisions tend to expand the scope of the word 'State’ as defined by _______ of the Indian Constitution.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Article 12**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Article 12:-**

 
 
• **The word 'State' is defined under Article 12 of the Indian Constitution, which includes the Government and Parliament of India, the Government and Legislature of each of the States, and all local or other authorities within the territory of India or under the control of the Government of India.**
 
• The scope of the word 'State' has been expanded by the judiciary to include private bodies or individuals performing public functions, which has led to the application of Fundamental Rights against them as well.

• It guarantees the right to equality before the law and equal protection of the laws within the territory of India.
 
 
 
• **Article 15:-**
 
 
• It prohibits discrimination on grounds of religion, race, caste, sex, or place of birth.
 
 
 
• **Article 13:-**
 
 
• It declares that any law that violates the Fundamental Rights shall be void.

questions.question: In the Indian Constitution the concept of 'equality before law' is borrowed from the ______ constitution.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**British**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Equality before law:-**

 
 
• The concept of 'equality before law' in the Indian constitution is borrowed from the British constitution.
 
• The principle of equality before law means that everyone, regardless of their status, wealth, religion, or caste, is equal before the law and subject to the same laws and penalties.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Canadian constitution:-**

 
 
• The Canadian constitution has its own unique provisions on equality, including the Charter of Rights and Freedoms, which guarantees equal protection and benefit of the law without discrimination based on race, national or ethnic origin, colour, religion, sex, age, or mental or physical disability.
 
 
 
• **US constitution:-**
 
 
• The US constitution also has provisions on equality, including the Fourteenth Amendment, which guarantees equal protection of the laws to all citizens and prohibits discrimination based on race, color, or national origin.
 
 
 
• **Irish constitution:-**
 
 
• The Irish constitution also has provisions on equality, including the principle of equal treatment under the law and the prohibition of discrimination based on age, disability, gender, race, or sexual orientation.

questions.question: Which Article of the Indian Constitution mentions that laws that are inconsistent with or in derogation of any of the fundamental rights shall be void?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Article 13**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Article 13 of the Indian Constitution:-**

 
 
• **It mentions that laws that are inconsistent with or in derogation of any of the fundamental rights shall be void.**
 
• This means that any law that goes against the fundamental rights guaranteed by the Constitution will be deemed invalid and unenforceable.
 
• Fundamental rights are an important aspect of the Indian Constitution and are enshrined in Part III of the Constitution.
 
• These rights include the right to equality, right to freedom, right against exploitation, right to freedom of religion, cultural and educational rights, and the right to constitutional remedies.
 
• The Constitution also provides for the protection of these fundamental rights through the mechanism of the judiciary, which can strike down any law that violates these rights. 
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Article 14 of the Constitution:-**

 
 
• It guarantees the right to equality before the law and equal protection of the law to all citizens.
 
 
 
• **Article 15:-**
 
 
• It prohibits discrimination on the grounds of religion, race, caste, sex or place of birth.
 
 
 
• **Article 16:-**
 
 
• It guarantees equality of opportunity in matters of public employment and prohibits discrimination on the grounds of religion, race, caste, sex, descent, place of birth, residence or any of them.
